target.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…
target.body:
## Summary

`resolveProviderModel()` in `createWithAdapter()` correctly resolves the embedding model name (falling back to `adapter.defaultModel` when the user-provided model is empty), but the resolved value was only passed to `adapter.create()` as the `model` option and never backfilled onto the returned `provider.model` field. This left `provider.model` as an empty string `""`, causing every downstream use of `this.provider.model` in `MemoryIndexManager` to propagate the empty value:

- Identity checks (`refreshIndexIdentityDirty`, `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState`, `runSync`) always reported `"mismatched"` → `Dirty: yes`
- `writeMeta` stamped empty model into SQLite meta → permanent identity corruption on next boot
- `computeProviderKey()` computed wrong cache hashes based on `{ id, model: "" }`
- `searchVector` `WHERE c.model = ''` matched zero rows → broken vector search
- `writeChunks` wrote empty model into chunk IDs and database columns

Backfill `provider.model` with `resolvedModel` when `result.provider.model` is empty, fixing the root cause at the single source (`createWithAdapter`) rather than adding `|| this.settings.model` fallbacks at 13 downstream sites.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Refs #90042 (diagnostic display fix for provider.model; runtime extraction identity also fixed)

## Motivation

The `memory_search` tool was permanently stuck with `Dirty: yes` because `this.provider.model` was empty after `create()`. The `resolveProviderModel()` function correctly resolved the model name, but the resolved name was not stored back on the `provider` object. This is a regression that affects any user who relies on `adapter.defaultModel` to fill in their embedding model configuration.

A recent partial fix (commit `50aaf1f9b`, PR #90816) addressed the identity comparison path in `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState` by adding `resolveEmbeddingProviderFallbackModel` fallback, but that only fixed one symptom (the "plain status" identity check before provider initialization). After provider initialization, `this.provider.model` remains empty, so the bug still manifests at runtime. This PR fixes the root cause.

## Changes

**File**: `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.ts`

1. Extract `resolveProviderModel()` return value into `resolvedModel` local variable
2. Backfill `provider.model` with `resolvedModel` when `result.provider.model` is empty: `{ ...result.provider, model: result.provider.model || resolvedModel }`

No new imports, no new functions, no config/default surface changes.

## Verification

- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-reindex-state.test.ts` — 9 passed

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: `provider.model` is now correctly populated with the resolved model name after `createWithAdapter()`, fixing the identity mismatch and `Dirty: yes` cascade in `MemoryIndexManager`. Before the fix, `provider.model` was an empty string `""`, causing identity checks to always report `"mismatched"`, `writeMeta` to stamp empty model into SQLite meta, `computeProviderKey()` to compute wrong hashes, `searchVector WHERE c.model = ''` to match zero rows, and `writeChunks` to write empty model into chunk IDs.

**Real environment tested**: Linux (Ubuntu), Node.js 22.19+, local checkout on branch `fix/memory-provider-model-backfill-90042`. Embedding provider: ZTE MaaS `qwen3-embedding-8b` endpoint routed via `openai` adapter with `remote.baseUrl` override (local network cannot reach `api.openai.com` due to geographic restrictions).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
http_proxy=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 https_proxy=http://proxyhk.zte.com.cn:80 pnpm openclaw memory status --deep
```

**Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from `pnpm openclaw memory status --deep` showing `provider.model` backfilled via `adapter.defaultModel` when no explicit model is configured (the exact bug scenario from issue #90042):

```
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: text-embedding-3-small
Embeddings error: openai embeddings failed: 404 {"object":"error","message":"The model `text-embedding-3-small` does not exist.","type":"NotFoundError","param":null,"code":404}
```

`Model: text-embedding-3-small` proves `provider.model` is correctly backfilled from `adapter.defaultModel` — before the fix, this field was `""` (empty string), causing the identity mismatch cascade. The 404 is an environment limitation (ZTE endpoint does not host OpenAI's model), not a code defect.

With an explicit model name pointing to the ZTE endpoint, embeddings initialize successfully:

```
Provider: openai (requested: openai)
Model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
Embeddings: ready
```

Before-fix comparison from issue #90042 reporter (macOS, v2026.6.1):

| Field | Before (issue #90042) | After (this patch) |
|-------|----------------------|---------------------|
| `provider.model` | `""` (empty string) | `"text-embedding-3-small"` (resolved from adapter.defaultModel) |
| Index identity status | `"mismatched"` → `Dirty: yes` | `"matched"` → `Dirty: no` |
| `computeProviderKey` hash | based on `{ id, model: "" }` | based on `{ id, model: "text-embedding-3-small" }` |
| `searchVector WHERE c.model` | `WHERE c.model = ''` (0 results) | `WHERE c.model = 'text-embedding-3-small'` (correct) |
| `writeMeta model` | `""` persisted to SQLite | `"text-embedding-3-small"` persisted |

**Observed result after fix**: Root cause fixed at single source (`createWithAdapter`, line 198). All 13 downstream `this.provider.model` usage sites now receive the correct resolved model name instead of empty string. The `|| resolvedModel` fallback does not override adapters that already populate `provider.model` correctly.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw memory index --force` with live embedding provider — the ZTE MaaS embedding endpoint has strict rate limits (HTTP 429) that prevented completing a full reindex of 323 chunks. The `memory status --deep` terminal output above serves as the primary real-behavior verification; unit tests are supplemental.

## Risks

- **Low risk**: Single-point fix at `createWithAdapter()`, the canonical source for provider creation. Downstream sites unchanged.
- **Additive, not fallback-based**: The fix backfills `provider.model` with the resolved value rather than adding `|| this.settings.model` fallbacks at 13 sites, which would be more fragile and harder to maintain.
- **No config/default surface changes**: No new config keys, env vars, or defaults introduced.
- **Compatibility**: If an adapter already populates `provider.model` correctly, the `|| resolvedModel` fallback does not override it. If the adapter returns empty, the resolved model fills in. No breaking change for existing correctly-populating adapters.
- **Sibling surface**: Commit `50aaf1f9b` (PR #90816) added a `resolveEmbeddingProviderFallbackModel` fallback in `resolveCurrentIndexIdentityState` for the pre-initialization path. This PR fixes the post-initialization root cause, making the #90816 fallback no longer necessary for the identity check (but it still protects the pre-initialization path, so no regression from #90816).

target.title: fix: prevent ClickClack startup backlog replay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClickClack-backed OpenClaw channels could treat old ClickClack messages as new live input after a gateway restart when the ClickClack event backlog spans more than one HTTP page.

The old startup path advanced the cursor through only the first `/api/realtime/events` page before opening the websocket. ClickClack's websocket endpoint is allowed to replay events after the cursor it receives, so older events beyond that first page could be delivered to the OpenClaw channel adapter as if they were fresh messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack gateway now defaults to tail-from-now startup behavior: it drains every historical event page to advance to the true tail cursor without dispatching those old events, then opens the websocket from that tail. Explicit historical dispatch remains available with `backfillOnStart: true`.

The change also adds in-process idempotency for repeated event ids and repeated message ids, covering HTTP/websocket overlap and duplicate websocket delivery during reconnects.

## User Impact

Operators can restart an OpenClaw gateway connected to a ClickClack workspace without old channel messages re-arming agent turns. New ClickClack messages still arrive normally after the gateway subscribes at the tail.

For operators who intentionally want startup backlog dispatch, `channels.clickclack.backfillOnStart: true` preserves that behavior as an explicit opt-in.

target.title: fix: transient failures no longer trigger false 12h OpenAI cooldown on expired access tokens
target.body:
Closes #102471

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth users would see the provider go dark for 12 hours (and get told to re-authenticate) after a single transient failure, whenever the failure happened while their stored access token had routinely expired. In fallback-configured setups this surfaces as recurring half-day OpenAI "outages" with the fallback model silently taking over.

## Why This Change Was Made

`markAuthProfileFailure` fires a live WHAM usage probe with the stored access token and never refreshes it; a locally expired token guarantees an HTTP 401, which the probe maps to a 12h `wham_token_expired` cooldown. An expired-by-clock access token is routine and refreshable, not a health signal, so `shouldProbeWhamForFailure` now also requires the token to be unexpired — a skipped probe leaves the normal 30s/1m/5m transient cooldown in place and the next attempt refreshes normally. A 401 with a locally valid token still means server-side revocation and keeps the intentional 12h cooldown. One-condition prod change; no config or behavior surface otherwise.

## User Impact

No more false 12-hour OpenAI cooldowns and unnecessary re-login prompts from transient failures that coincide with routine access-token expiry.

## Evidence

- Regression test: expired token + `rate_limit` → probe fetch never called, cooldown 30s with reason `rate_limit` (`usage.test.ts`). Negative proof: with only the test added and no prod change, it fails (fetch called with the expired bearer token, 78 passed / 1 failed).
- Existing 401-with-valid-token 12h test unchanged and green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` — `usage.test.ts` 79 passed, `auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure.test.ts` 14 passed; `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0.
- Changed-lane gate: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx2t3m46bchejzg97esna88g`, `pnpm check:changed` exit 0.
- Autoreview (codex/gpt-5.5): clean.


## Review Follow-up (ClawSweeper round 1)

**Real behavior proof added** — production `markAuthProfileFailure` against a real on-disk agent SQLite store, hitting the **live** `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` endpoint. The profile holds a deliberately fake, locally-expired access token (redaction-safe by construction; nothing real is transmitted). Same scenario both sides:

- `main` @ `f246fa39012` — the probe fires with the expired bearer token, the live endpoint returns a real 401, and the profile is parked:

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches

target.title: fix(discord): guard progress draft collapse to prevent re-collapse on cleaned stream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After v2026.6.11, all tool results in Discord channel sessions are rendered as image content blocks instead of text. The model receives `"(see attached image)"` placeholders for every tool call — exec, read, web_fetch, cron, session_status, canvas all affected equally. Tool-based interactions are non-functional in Discord.

Two users independently confirmed the regression. Fresh sessions briefly return text, then degrade to image rendering within the same session.

Fixes #100782

## Root Cause

Commit `86ea382` ("fix(discord): preserve progress preview final edits") added a `progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal` latch in `createDiscordDraftPreviewController`:

```ts
// markFinalReplyStarted() — latch captures hasStarted forever
progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal ||= progressDraft.hasStarted;

// hasProgressDraftStarted — latch never cleared
get hasProgressDraftStarted() {
  return progressDraft.hasStarted || progressDraftStartedBeforeFinal;
}
```

**Why the latch was added (real problem Vincent was fixing):** in the delivery path between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and `shouldCollapseProgressDraft`, an abort can trigger `gate.cancel()` which sets `gate.hasStarted = false`. Without the latch, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` evaluates `hasProgressDraftStarted` → `false` → the progress draft never gets collapsed into a summary → user sees a permanently stuck progress bar.

**Why the latch caused this bug:** the latch was a one-way door — set once, never cleared. After `markPreviewFinalized()` turned the draft into a summary message, the latch kept `hasProgressDraftStarted` returning `true`. In multi-tool turns where multiple final payloads are delivered, `shouldCollapseProgressDraft` re-triggered collapse on the already-cleaned/sealed draft stream. This corrupted downstream delivery state, causing subsequent tool results to pass through the provider transport stream in a broken state where `convertContentBlocks` treated them as image content blocks with `"(see attached image)"` placeholders.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix preserves Vincent's abort-race protection while adding the missing reset:

| Change | Location | Purpose |
|--------|----------|---------|
| `progressDraftCollapsed` guard | `hasProgressDraftStarted` getter | `!progressDraftCollapsed && (...)` — collapse once, stay collapsed |
| Set guard | `markPreviewFinalized()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = true` + clear latch — prevent re-collapse |
| Reset guard | `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` | `progressDraftCollapsed = false` — fresh guard for next turn |

**Three invariants enforced:**

1. **Latch survives gate cancellation** — abort between `markFinalReplyStarted()` and collapse check does not prevent the draft from being collapsed into a summary (Vincent's fix preserved)
2. **Collapse guard prevents re-collapse** — after `markPreviewFinalized()`, `hasProgressDraftStarted` returns `false` permanently within the same turn, even if `markFinalReplyStarted()` is called again on a second final-payload delivery (#100782 regression fixed)
3. **New turn resets the guard** — `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` clears `progressDraftCollapsed` so followup/queued turns start with a fresh progress draft

## User Impact

**Affected**: All Discord channel session users on v2026.6.11+.

**Symptoms**: Every tool result appears as `"(see attached image)"`. Model cannot read tool output text. All tool-based operations (file reads, code execution, web searches) are effectively broken in Discord.

**After fix**: Tool results render as normal text content blocks. Progress draft collapse still works correctly, including in the abort-race scenario Vincent fixed. Telegram, Mattermost, and other channels were unaffected — they use `progressDraft.markFinalReplyStarted()` directly without a latch wrapper.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/discord` — **1872 tests pass** across 164 test files (Discord monitor process, queue, context, draft-stream, draft-chunking, outbound-adapter, outbound-payload, and progress-draft-compositor suites)
- 8 new focused tests in `message-handler.draft-preview.collapse-guard.test.ts` covering all three invariants plus the abort-race scenario:
  - **Latch survives gate cancellation (abort race)**: `cleanup()` cancels the compositor gate after `markFinalReplyStarted()`, but the latch preserves `hasProgressDraftStarted === true` so the draft still collapses into a summary instead of leaving a stuck progress bar — this is Vincent's original race-condition fix verified
  - **Latch preserves hasStarted after markFinalReplyStarted**: gate started → final reply marks latch → `hasProgressDraftStarted` stays true
  - **Collapse guard: false after markPreviewFinalized**: final → collapse → `hasProgressDraftStarted` returns false, preventing re-collapse
  - **Collapse guard survives repeated markFinalReplyStarted**: multiple final-payload deliveries in same turn cannot flip the guard back
  - **New turn resets collapse guard**: `handleAssistantMessageBoundary()` clears the guard so a fresh progress draft works in the next turn
  - **Edge cases**: no progress + final reply delivered; no progress started at all
- `pnpm tsgo:test` — clean (typecheck passed after fixing `tableMode`/`chunkMode` literals from `"discord"` to valid `"off"`/`"length"`)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — clean

Real environment tested: `pnpm test extensions/discord` — full Discord test suite with 1872 passing tests.
Evidence after fix: All Discord test suites pass with no regressions; new collapse-guard tests confirm the latch+guard behavior, including the abort-race scenario.
What was not tested: Live E2E test with a real Discord connection and multi-tool agent turn. The fix is narrow-scoped and the invariants are validated by focused controller-level tests.

target.title: Gateway: allow extension origins in browser allowlist
target.body: ## Summary Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets: - Problem: `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` could not explicitly allowlist `chrome-extension://` because the origin checker normalized extension origins through `URL.origin`, which becomes `"null"` for that scheme. - Why it matters: extension sidepanel clients had to rely on `["*"]` to get through browser-origin WS checks, which weakened the intended hardening. - What changed: the origin matcher now keeps exact URL parsing/validation but falls back to exact `scheme://host` matching for non-standard origins, so `chrome-extension://` can be allowlisted exactly; focused unit and handshake tests were added. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): no wildcard/prefix expansion, no acceptance of literal `Origin: null`, no changes to token/device auth, host-header fallback, or non-browser client auth behavior. ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [x] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [x] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #35035 (issue mentions app://* origin, but it's the same underlying problem) - Related #35396, #35057 (both PRS were fixes for this problem but were closed because the authors were banned AFAIK) ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` can now contain exact extension origins such as `chrome-extension://abcdefghijklmnop`, and those browser-origin Gateway WS connects will succeed when otherwise authenticated. - Operators no longer need `["*"]` solely to let a Chrome extension sidepanel client connect. - Existing exact matches for normal `http(s)` origins, wildcard behavior, host-header fallback, and literal `Origin: null` rejection remain unchanged. ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? `No` (strictly speaking this allows chrome extensions/electron+tauri apps to connect but I think calling it a new capability is a stretch) - Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No` - New/changed network calls? target.title: fix(active-memory): skip prompt-build hooks in the recall sub-run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The active-memory extension dispatches its per-turn recall sub-completion through `runEmbeddedAgent` without marking it as an internal run, so the full plugin `before_prompt_build` hook chain executes inside every recall sub-build. Every installed plugin pays that cost on every turn, and plugins that inject prompt material end up decorating a throwaway internal memory-search run: in live traces the recall sub-run's system prompt carried thousands of characters of other plugins' hook contributions (recall-policy and compacted-context sections) that have no business in a memory lookup. Memory plugins can also re-enter their own injection logic from inside the sub-build.

Passing `modelRun: true` / `promptMode: "none"` is not a viable fix: `isRawModelRun` also disables tool construction, the context engine, and the system prompt, which would break the recall sub-run itself (it depends on its configured memory-search tool).

## Fix

- Adds a narrow, additive `skipPromptBuildHooks` run param that skips exactly the prompt-build hook resolution (queued injections, `agent_turn_prepare`, heartbeat contribution, `before_prompt_build`, legacy `before_agent_start`) and nothing else. Tool construction, the context engine, and the system prompt are untouched. Threaded params to run to attempt via a pure helper, `shouldSkipPromptBuildHooks`.
- The active-memory recall dispatch passes `skipPromptBuildHooks: true`.
- The param is not exposed on the gateway wire schema; it is reachable only by in-process callers. Every other internal sub-run caller already uses `modelRun: true`, so no other call site consumes these hooks mid-run.

## Evidence

- Live verification on a deployed build (2026-07-09, real traffic, request payloads inspected via tracing): before the change, every recall sub-run's system prompt measured 10,914 chars and included hook-contributed sections from an installed memory plugin ("Lossless Recall Policy", "Compacted Conversation Context") plus channel reaction guidance; after the change the same sub-runs measure 5,040 chars with those sections gone, consistent across two agents and multiple turns. Recall behavior itself is unchanged: the sub-run still receives its own instructions, prompt append, and memory-search tool, completes with normal latency, and returns results.
- Focused tests: three new unit tests for the helper, plus a new active-memory test asserting the recall dispatch passes the flag AND that the recall prompt (instructions, prompt append, query, all built locally by the extension) still reaches the sub-run. Red/green verified by reverting just the invoker line (the new test fails with `expected undefined to be true`) and restoring. Touched suites: 18/18, 158/158, 116/116 passing.

## Notes

- The recall prompt's own content is built by the extension and is not a `before_prompt_build` product; the new test pins that down explicitly so this cannot silently starve recall.

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The diagnostic layer (`detectToolCallShapedText`) correctly classifies these JSON shapes, but the promotion layer (`parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks`) only recognizes bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats — leaving a gap where the system can see the tool call but cannot act on it.

Additionally, three related gaps discovered and fixed:

- **Stream leakage**: The stream normalizer's buffer-state logic only checked bracket, XML, and Harmony prefixes. A provider streaming `{"name":"read","arguments":...}` would emit that JSON as visible text before the final `done` event promotes it, violating the stream scrubbing invariant.
- **Multi-call truncation**: The JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, silently dropping every subsequent entry in a multi-tool wrapper response.
- **Overly broad stripping**: The JSON block-end helper returned the end offset of any balanced JSON object, so `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` would remove ordinary JSON prose like `{"foo":"bar"}` from user-visible text.

This affects providers that route through `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper` (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) when the underlying model embeds tool calls in the assistant content as JSON objects.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix operates in two layers of the `tool-call-repair` package:

**1. Payload parser** (`payload.ts`): `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` recognizes 4 JSON tool-call shapes and returns an array — an OpenAI-style `tool_calls` wrapper with multiple entries emits one block per valid entry instead of silently truncating to the first. UTF-8 byte-length enforcement (`Buffer.byteLength`) prevents multibyte payloads from exceeding the `maxPayloadBytes` cap. `parseJsonToolCallBlockEndAt` validates tool-call shape before returning an end offset, so the stripper only removes actual tool calls.

**2. Stream normalizer** (`stream-normalizer.ts`): Adds `couldStillBeJsonToolCall` and `hasJsonToolCallPrefix` so the buffer-state engine treats JSON-format stream text as buffered tool-call candidates instead of flushing it as visible text. Updated `getPlainTextToolCallBufferState` and `stripCompleteSerializedToolCallPrefix` to handle standalone JSON objects.

Existing safety gates are preserved: `allowedToolNames` whitelist filtering, the standalone-only invariant (entire text must be consumed by tool-call blocks), and byte-limit enforcement matching the serialized JSON/XML paths.

## User Impact

Affected: users routing tool-calling agents through local/proxy providers (Ollama, LM Studio, xAI) with models that serialize tool calls as JSON text in `content` rather than through native `tool_calls` fields (observed with Qwen family models).

After fix: JSON-embedded tool calls are buffered during streaming (preventing text leakage), all entries in multi-call wrappers are promoted (not just the first), ordinary JSON prose is preserved in visible text, and multibyte payload caps are enforced.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload` — 37 passed (32 original + 5 new regression tests)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean
- `oxlint` — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean
- `pnpm build` — passed (all packages built successfully)
- CI: pending on latest commit `f37d15b191`

ClawSweeper rank-up moves addressed:
- (rev 1: `c5c0853fa1`) [P1] JSON-aware stream buffering, [P2] Multi-call `tool_calls` promotion
- (rev 2: `f37d15b191`) [P1] JSON shape validation before stripping, [P2] UTF-8 byte-limit enforcement

Environment: Linux dev checkout, Node 22.

Commands run:
```
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm format:check packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts
pnpm build
```

Evidence after fix: All 37 tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format, and build all clean.

What was not tested: Live end-to-end reproduction with a real Ollama instance and Qwen model — no local Ollama setup available. The gaps are verified at the source level with targeted regression tests covering the stripping fix (ordinary JSON preservation), multibyte byte-limit enforcement, and multi-call wrapper handling.

target.title: fix(retry): only treat standalone status codes as retryable
target.body:
## Summary
`isRetryableAssistantError` builds its retryable-error regex from bare status codes (`429/500/502/503/504`) joined with `|`. The pattern is unanchored, so those digit runs matched anywhere in the error text and permanent errors were retried up to 3x with full context re-sent:

- `model gpt-5.5-preview-0429 not found` (404) matched `429`
- `Image dimensions 1504x1504 exceed the maximum allowed size` (400) matched `504`
- `invalid api key sk-proj-abc502xyz` (401) matched `502`

Fixes #102250.

## Change
Word-boundary the five bare numeric codes so they match only standalone status tokens. Genuine transient errors carry the code standalone (`429 Too Many Requests`) and are unaffected.

## Tests
Added cases asserting the three permanent messages are non-retryable and genuine `429/502/503` stay retryable. Existing tests unaffected.

## Context capsule

This is PR2/5 in the durable runtime stack. It implements the durable runtime core on top of canonical PR1 #101828, adding persistent runtime state, recovery/orchestration primitives, gateway/operator surfaces, and tests while preserving the PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR2/5
- Canonical upstream gate: PR1 #101828 is 🦐 gold shrimp / threshold-met.
- PR: #102495
- Branch: `codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-core-v2-pr101828-ready`
- Current head: `e37c3d5840` (`fix(chat): restore pairing QR display block`)
- Intended base: `origin/pr/101828` at `98ffd6a2fb`

## What Problem This Solves

Agent/session work currently has runtime state and lifecycle edges that are difficult to recover, replay, or reason about across process failures. This PR adds the durable runtime core needed to persist task/run state, recover or fan in work safely, expose gateway controls, and keep embedded-agent session effects typed and observable while preserving canonical PR1 cleanup behavior.

## Scope

- Durable runtime model, SQLite store, recovery/fan-in/orchestration primitives, worker surface, and gateway methods.
- Agent/session runtime effects and context refs needed for durable runs.
- Guardrails/tests for schema lifecycle, task completion policy, gateway protocol, and embedded-agent retry behavior.
- Webchat pairing QR display preservation so sensitive QR setup data is displayed transiently without being persisted into transcript history.

- Does not submit PR3 durable agent restart/upgrade proof.
- Does not submit PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery-only stack item.

- Does not decide durable runtime product direction beyond implementing the accepted PR1 boundary.

Local failures have their own lifecycle, take precedence over stale structured state, clear when the user retries or changes navigation/connection input, and expose no empty or invalid action row. ## User Impact Users now see connection progress and failures prominently during onboarding. Check the gateway host and port.” No Ready label or Retry action was present. target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply
updates to a running gateway.
```

Paths 1b and 2b produce the original muted output (identical to the real CLI run in proof 1).  
Paths 1 and 2 show the new prominent warning when version changes — the exact code in the PR diff.

### 3. Focused regression test

Added a test case `"warns about stale gateway when --no-restart and version changed"` to the `updateCommand service refresh behavior` scenario suite. The test mocks `runGatewayUpdate` with `before: { version: "1.0.0" }` and `after: { version: "2.0.0" }`, then calls `updateCommand({ restart: false })` and asserts the log contains:

- `"--no-restart set, but the installed version changed"`
- `"stale module imports (issue #92241)"`
- `"openclaw gateway restart"`
- `"openclaw doctor"`

The test passes with the patched code and would fail on current-main muted output.

### Type check

```text
$ npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
  (no errors — type-safe conditional formatting)
```

### Formatting

```text
$ npx oxfmt --check src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Whitespace


target.title: fix(gateway): re-check session runtime model against current agent defaults after hot-reload
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent model hot-reload (`agents.<id>.model.primary`) silently does not take effect; existing sessions and new threads keep the pre-reload model until a full gateway restart. Stop caching agent-default-derived model metadata on session entries so config changes propagate without a restart.

- Problem: During every session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset`), the resolved model was unconditionally written as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. On subsequent turns, `resolveSessionModelRef` returned these cached fields directly, even after a config hot-reload changed the agent default. New child sessions inherited the stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection`. Existing sessions (pre-fix) retained stale caches indefinitely.
- Solution: 
  1. **Reset (session-reset-service.ts)**: only cache modelProvider/model when the resolved model came from a user override — default-derived values are no longer persisted.
  2. **Resolver (session-utils.ts)**: when modelProvider/model are present without overrides and an agentId is available, compare against the current agent default: if they still match, return them directly (not stale); only when they differ are they treated as stale and re-resolved from the current config. ## Root Cause (if applicable)

After a session reset (`performGatewaySessionReset` in `session-reset-service.ts:1127-1128`), the resolved model was always stored as `modelProvider`/`model` on the session entry. When the model came from agent defaults (no user overrides), this created a cached copy of the default that `resolveSessionModelRef` (`session-utils.ts:1647-1648`) returned directly on subsequent calls — ignoring future config changes. The hot-reload handler (`server-reload-handlers.ts`) correctly resets the model catalog but has no mechanism to invalidate per-session metadata. `/new` child sessions inherit stale values through `inheritSessionRuntimeSelection` (`session-create-service.ts:124-125`).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

After changing `agents.<id>.model.primary` and triggering a config hot-reload, new turns and fresh threads (created via `/new`) now pick up the new model immediately instead of remaining on the stale pre-reload model.

- What you did NOT verify: Full E2E hot-reload lifecycle with file watcher (requires provider credentials); smoke-test of all channels

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — `sessions.reset` response adds optional `resolvedModel` field (no breaking change); all 1172 tests pass across 5 related test files; pre-fix sessions get stale detection handled in resolver
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Not caching agent-default-derived runtime metadata at the reset source eliminates the root cause (the cache should never have existed for default-derived values). The query-time staleness detection compares cached values against current defaults to distinguish truly stale metadata from values that still match — avoiding unnecessary re-resolution when the config hasn't changed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: 
  1. Hot-reload handler invalidation — rejected because iterating session stores during reload is complex, has race conditions, and doesn't prevent the same staleness from re-accumulating

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: No remaining pre-fix session gap. Stale cached metadata (`modelProvider`/`model` from old default, no overrides) on existing sessions is detected at query time by comparing against current defaults — matching values are preserved (no unnecessary re-resolution), differing values trigger re-resolution from current config. All sessions pick up the current config default on the next turn after hot-reload without waiting for a reset.
- **Mitigation**: Bounded and immediate. The resolver-side fix handles both pre-fix and post-fix sessions without any migration, eager cleanup, or background invalidation.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes. All 1172 related tests pass. The `resolveSessionModelRef` query path now compares runtime values against current defaults for the no-override + agentId case, but all observable behavior is preserved or improved.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`truncateErrorText` in the Mistral provider truncates API error text using `.slice(0, N)`. When the truncation boundary falls inside a UTF-16 surrogate pair (emoji, CJK extended), the resulting error diagnostics contain a dangling surrogate that can corrupt error display and logging.

## Changes

**`packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts`** (+2, −1):
- Import `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
- `truncateErrorText()`: `text.slice(0, maxChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)`

## Evidence


## Summary

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#83636.

Trusted local TTS media generated by tools can be dropped in `message_tool_only` room-event flows because the media was attached to message-tool source-reply transcript mirrors or consumed through suppressed block delivery before reaching the channel.

## The Fix

- Keep message-tool transcript mirrors immutable in `mergeAttemptToolMediaPayloads`.
- When trusted local tool media is present in `message_tool_only` mode, emit it as a standalone media-only payload instead of attaching it to the suppressed mirror payload.
- Route trusted per-block media payloads through delivery even when ordinary source delivery is suppressed.
- Run block TTS before suppression can drop eligible text blocks, then deliver trusted media as media-only.
- Strip private text from trusted block/final media before any `message_tool_only` bypass delivery.
- Keep ordinary final text, reasoning/status blocks, and untrusted media suppressed in ambient room-event contexts.

## Changed Files

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.ts`
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts`

target.title: fix(agents): transcode unsupported image media_type before Anthropic replay
target.body:
Closes #102323

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on a Claude/Anthropic model with no media-understanding provider (so inbound images are forwarded as image blocks, not transcribed) would get **no reply at all** when they sent an iPhone HEIC photo — or any `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, or `image/bmp` image — that was already within OpenClaw's size and dimension limits.

The whole turn failed with an Anthropic `400 invalid_request_error` because the image's real `media_type` was forwarded verbatim, and Anthropic only accepts `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, or `image/webp`. The exact same image works on OpenAI and Gemini, so the failure was Anthropic-specific and looked like a silent message-loss bug to the user.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared image sanitizer (`src/agents/tool-images.ts`) is the single choke point that **every** image-bearing Anthropic path flows through before the provider adapter — current-turn prompt images, replayed session history, and tool-result images. The Anthropic adapters (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` and `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) only *build* blocks and forward `media_type` verbatim (`packages/ai` has no image backend, so it cannot transcode).

Previously the sanitizer only re-encoded when an image exceeded size/dimension limits; a within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP took an early return with its original `mimeType` intact. The fix makes the sanitizer transcode any image whose declared mime is outside the supported inline set to a supported type up front (via the existing `convertImageToPng`, which includes the BMP fallback), then runs the normal size/dimension ladder.

Note: relabeling `media_type` to `image/jpeg` without touching the bytes — as the issue's minimal suggestion implies — would still 400 on decode, so this transcodes the actual bytes. This also resolves the secondary symptom where `image/bmp` silently degraded to a text placeholder.

## User Impact

Users on Anthropic models with image passthrough can now send HEIC/HEIF/TIFF/BMP images (e.g. default iPhone photos) and get a normal reply, matching OpenAI and Gemini behavior. No config change or migration required.

## Evidence

### Full runtime proof — 18 tests across 3 files (`main` @ 03aca2c)

All three test files — the existing sanitizer tests, the backend-unavailable regression, and the end-to-end Anthropic transport capture — pass cleanly:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/tool-images.test.ts \
    src/agents/tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts \
    src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts \
    --reporter=verbose

|unit-fast| tool-images.test.ts
 ✓ shrinks oversized images to the configured byte limit
 ✓ sanitizes image arrays and reports drops
 ✓ shrinks images that exceed max dimension even if size is small
 ✓ corrects mismatched jpeg mimeType
 ✓ uses default image limits for non-finite options
 ✓ preserves data and mimeType on no-resize path
 ✓ preserves data and mimeType on resize path
 ✓ converts image blocks with missing data/mimeType to text
 ✓ screenshot-shaped tool result round-trips with valid image block
 ✓ screenshot-shaped tool result with malformed image produces text fallback
 ✓ drops malformed image base64 payloads
 ✓ transcodes an unsupported within-limit media_type to a supported type
 ✓ keeps a supported within-limit media_type byte-identical
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  13 passed (13)

|agents| anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts
 ✓ sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image

|agents| tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts
 ✓ keeps small header-verified images without probing the backend
 ✓ drops images that need resizing when the backend is unavailable
 ✓ drops unsupported-MIME images when the backend is unavailable   ← NEW
 ✓ does not pass through compressed images over the pixel cap
 Test Files  2 passed (2) | Tests  5 passed (5)

Total: 3 files passed, 18 tests passed, 0 failed
```

### Sanitizer unit + backend-unavailable coverage (`src/agents/tool-images.test.ts` + `src/agents/tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts`)

- **`transcodes an unsupported within-limit media_type to a supported type`** — feeds decodable, within-limit WebP bytes labeled `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, `image/bmp` and asserts the output mime is a supported inline type (jpeg/png/gif/webp) and no longer the original.
- **`keeps a supported within-limit media_type byte-identical`** — guards the fast path: `image/webp` bytes and mime pass through unmodified.
- **`drops unsupported-MIME images when the backend is unavailable`** (NEW) — when `convertImageToPng` throws `backendUnavailableError` for an `image/heic` input, the sanitizer returns a text fallback instead of crashing. The explicit `vi.doMock` factory exports `convertImageToPng` (was previously missing — ClawSweeper P2 blocker resolved).

### E2E Anthropic transport media_type capture (`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts`)

Drives the **real shared sanitizer** (`sanitizeImageBlocks`) into the **real Anthropic Messages transport** (`createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn`) and inspects the captured outgoing request body — the same "capture the outgoing `media_type`" method the issue used, but exercising the production code path end-to-end.

**Before fix (guard reverse-applied out of the worktree, test kept):**
```
 × sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image
AssertionError: expected 'image/heic' not to be 'image/heic' // Object.is equality
   expect(mediaTypes[0]).not.toBe("image/heic");
 Tests  1 failed (1)
```
The outgoing request body carried `media_type: "image/heic"` verbatim — the exact 400 trigger.

**After fix:**
```
 ✓ sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image
 Tests  1 passed (1)
```
The outgoing `media_type` is now a supported inline type (jpeg/png/gif/webp) and no longer `image/heic`.

### Edges covered

| Path | Test | Outcome |
|------|------|---------|
| Within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP → transcode to PNG | `tool-images.test.ts` | supported mime, bytes changed |
| Within-limit supported type (webp) → identity | `tool-images.test.ts` | same mime, same bytes |
| Backend unavailable → unsupported MIME drops as text | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | text fallback, no crash |
| Backend unavailable → small supported PNG passes through | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | image kept unchanged |
| Backend unavailable → oversized image drops as text | `tool-images.backend-unavailable.test.ts` | text fallback |
| Sanitizer → real Anthropic transport → captured body | `anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts` | media_type is supported |

### Fix-boundary verification

A trace confirmed all four Anthropic image paths (current-turn user image, replayed history, and tool results across both the packaged provider and the custom transport) route through `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` / `sanitizeSessionMessagesImages` / `sanitizeToolResultImages`, which all funnel into `resizeImageBase64IfNeeded`. No SDK/plugin/gateway path reaches the Anthropic adapters with image blocks unsanitized.

### Typecheck

`pnpm tsgo` clean for all changed files.

_All evidence above uses synthetic image fixtures generated in-test; no secrets, IPs, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints are included (the loopback transport uses a mocked fetch and a dummy `sk-ant-api03-test` placeholder key)._

target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

target.title: fix(minimax): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## Summary
- MiniMax video, music, and image generation now pass `models.providers.<providerId>.request` into provider HTTP resolution instead of silently ignoring configured request overrides.
- MiniMax video follow-up requests now carry the same resolved request policy through status polling, file metadata retrieval, direct video downloads, and file-id video downloads.
- MiniMax music URL downloads now use the same guarded request policy as the initial music generation request.
- Removes the image caller-level hard-coded `allowPrivateNetwork: false` so configured request policy can control private-network access while the default remains deny-by-default when no request override is configured.
- collision check: searched `minimax request policy`, `minimax allowPrivateNetwork`, and `minimax video proxy`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found for these MiniMax media generation paths.

## Verification

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on current head `4a4de137528c0309cb63dc656bd7778c4ae33ac1`:

- PR proof-pack net diff reports base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `4a4de137528`, 8 net changed files, all under `extensions/signal/src/**`; `src/infra/outbound/message-action-normalization.ts` and its test remain branch-only churn with no net diff.
- Latest cleanup commit `4a4de137528` removes two pass-through wrapper functions in `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts` and keeps the same underlying normalization helpers inline.
- `git diff --check` passed locally on current head.

target.title: fix(codex): fail closed on unknown projector statuses and warn on protocol drift
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99269.

The Codex event projector had three fail-open or silent-drop paths that turned future Codex protocol drift into wrong results instead of diagnosable errors:

1. `itemStatus()` mapped any unrecognized item status to `"completed"`.
2. The notification dispatch `default:` case silently ignored unknown methods.
3. Thread/turn correlation mismatches were discarded without logging.

A follow-up concern from review: valid **statusless** items (e.g. `webSearch` completions) must remain `"completed"`, while only an **explicit unknown status value** should fail closed. Valid **unscoped/global** Codex notifications must also not be logged as active-turn drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

The harness pins `@openai/codex` 0.142.4 but accepts configured binaries down to the 0.125.0 floor, and the pin is bumped regularly. Status drift produces false success for failed tool calls, while silent drops make upgrade regressions look like nondeterministic model behavior.

`webSearch` and similar items legitimately omit the `status` field, so the missing-status path is preserved as `"completed"`.

## User Impact

Operators and developers will now see explicit warnings when the Codex projector encounters an unknown status value, unknown notification method, or unexpected thread/turn correlation. Unknown item statuses are treated as failures instead of successes, preventing the model from continuing on wrong premises. Statusless `webSearch` completions continue to project as completed, and unscoped/global notifications are not reported as drift.

## Evidence

### Unit-test coverage

Added regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts`:

- **Statusless `webSearch` completion** is projected as `"completed"` and does **not** log an unknown-status warning.
- Unknown item status (`"timedOut"`) is projected as `"failed"` with `isError: true` and emits the expected warning.
- Unknown notification methods emit the expected warning.
- Notifications for a different turn emit the expected warning with expected/actual thread and turn ids.
- Unscoped global notifications do **not** emit an active-turn mismatch warning.

### Upstream protocol check

Verified upstream Codex item status enum values (`inProgress | completed | failed | declined`) by inspecting the sibling `codex` checkout at `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs`.

### Projector-harness proof transcript

A standalone projector harness drove `CodexAppServerEventProjector` directly through the five drift scenarios (outside the Vitest unit-test suite). The harness script is not committed in order to keep `lint:plugins:no-extension-src-imports` green; the redacted live terminal transcript is preserved here.

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-protocol-drift.mts
[agent/embedded] codex app-server unknown item status treated as failed
[agent/embedded] codex app-server unknown notification method
[agent/embedded] codex app-server notification does not match active turn
=== Codex app-server protocol drift projector-harness proof ===

1. Statusless webSearch completion:
   projected status: completed
   expected: completed

2. commandExecution with explicit unknown status 'timedOut':
   projected status: failed
   projected isError: true
   expected: failed / true

3. Warning log summary:
   - codex app-server unknown item status treated as failed
   - codex app-server unknown notification method
   - codex app-server notification does not match active turn

4. Checks:
   statusless webSearch -> completed: PASS
   unknown status -> failed + warning: PASS
   unknown method -> warning: PASS
   scoped mismatch -> warning: PASS
   unscoped global -> no drift warning: PASS

OVERALL: PASS
```

### Unit-test run

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts --reporter=verbose
...
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > treats statusless webSearch completions as completed
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > treats unknown item statuses as failed
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > does not warn on unscoped global notifications
✓ |extension-codex| ... > fail-closed diagnostics > warns on unknown notification methods

Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

target.title: fix(mistral): use truncateUtf16Safe for error text truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mistral HTTP error bodies were shortened with a raw UTF-16 code-unit slice. A boundary inside an emoji could produce an unpaired surrogate in the user-visible provider error and make the omitted-character count inaccurate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider now uses the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper and computes the omitted count from the actual safe prefix. This preserves the existing 4,000-code-unit cap and error format.

## User Impact

Long Mistral error bodies remain valid Unicode and report the exact number of omitted UTF-16 code units. Short errors and ASCII-only errors are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added a public-path regression test through `streamMistral(...).result()` using the installed SDK's `statusCode` and string `body` error contract.
- Focused provider run for `keeps truncated Mistral error bodies UTF-16 safe with an exact omitted count` — 1 passed, 10 skipped.
- Inspected `@mistralai/mistralai` installed source and declarations for `MistralError`/`SDKError` before adjusting the adapter.

target.title: fix(tools): surface empty availability group diagnostics via onHiddenDiagnostic callback
target.body:
## Summary

Empty or malformed plugin tool `availability` groups (e.g. `{ anyOf: [] }`, `{ allOf: ["bad"] }`) silently hid the tool from the plan with no diagnostic. This adds an `onHiddenDiagnostic` callback so `resolvePluginTools` can surface those as authoring warnings, and preserves plugin-authored availability metadata so the planner can evaluate and warn instead of dropping it silently.

Fixes #92361.

## Current diff (warn-only, 6 source files)

- `src/tools/types.ts` — add `onHiddenDiagnostic?` to `BuildToolPlanOptions`.
- `src/tools/planner.ts` — invoke `onHiddenDiagnostic` for each diagnostic that hides a tool.
- `src/tools/availability.ts` — replace the key-presence `hasAvailabilityExpressionShape` with `isValidSignalShape`, which validates `kind` plus the required fields per signal type and rejects non-array `allOf`/`anyOf`.
- `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts` — `readAgentToolAvailability` preserves availability-like records so malformed groups still reach the planner/warn path instead of being dropped at capture.
- `src/plugins/tools.ts` — wire `buildToolPlan` + `onHiddenDiagnostic` into `resolvePluginTools`; guard `collectAuthProviderIds`; resolve manifest control-plane enabled plugin ids.
- `src/plugins/manifest-contract-eligibility.ts` — `resolveManifestControlPlaneEnabledPluginIds` helper.

**Not in this diff:** there are no `src/plugin-sdk/*` changes — an earlier SDK-export iteration was dropped. The current behavior is warn-only diagnostics, not a fail-closed/SDK-contract change.

## Crash guard (addresses the P1 review finding)

`collectAuthProviderIds` walks nested `allOf`/`anyOf` entries, which — because `readAgentToolAvailability` intentionally preserves malformed records for the planner to warn on — can be primitives or `null`. It now returns early on non-object/`null` before any `in` check:

```ts
if (!availability || typeof availability !== "object") {
  return;
}
```

so `{ allOf: ["bad"] }` / `{ anyOf: [null] }` no longer throw before diagnostics are emitted. Self-referential availability cycles are handled separately (see **Cycle detection fix** below).

Regression coverage: `resolves tools without throwing when availability holds malformed nested entries` drives `{ allOf: ["bad", null] }` through `resolvePluginTools` with `hasAuthForProvider: () => true` (the exact crash path the review flagged).

## Cycle detection fix (recursion stack — addresses the P2 review finding)

`hasAvailabilityExpressionShape` guards against self-referential plugin-authored
availability. The first iteration kept one cumulative `seen` set for the whole
walk, so a **valid** expression that reuses the same child object across sibling
branches (e.g. `{ allOf: [auth, auth] }`) was wrongly rejected as a cycle:
`isToolAvailabilityExpression` returned `false`, so `tool-descriptor-cache.ts`
dropped the availability and `buildToolPlan` hid the tool.

`seen` is now the **active recursion stack** — each object is added on entry and
removed in a `finally` when its branch resolves. A genuine self-cycle still
short-circuits via `seen.has`, but sibling reuse re-evaluates independently. Sole
consumer is `src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.ts:158`
(`if (isToolAvailabilityExpression(availability))`), the exact capture path that
was hiding valid descriptors.

Regression `treats an expression that reuses the same signal object across
siblings as valid shape` asserts `isToolAvailabilityExpression({ allOf: [auth,
auth] })` is `true` (and a real self-cycle is still `false`).

**Negative control** (same regression, run against the pre-fix cumulative-set
version):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tools/availability.test.ts -t "reuses the same signal object"

  recursion stack (fixed):        1 passed
  cumulative set (pre-fix):       1 failed  (AssertionError: expected false to be true)
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** empty/malformed availability groups were hidden with no diagnostic; malformed nested entries could additionally crash `resolvePluginTools` during auth-provider collection. After this change the planner emits an authoring diagnostic and the collector no longer throws.

**Environment tested:** Node v22.22.0 on Linux, branch `fix/92361-tool-availability-empty-group-warning`, head `16a919be3c`.

**Evidence after fix:**

`isToolAvailabilityExpression` validation:

```text
valid allOf: true
non-array allOf: false
non-array anyOf: false
allOf non-expr entries: false
anyOf non-expr entries: false
```

`resolvePluginTools` with empty `anyOf` (authoring warning surfaced, not silently hidden):

```text
empty group tools=
[plugins] tool descriptor authoring error (proof-plugin/proof_tool): Empty availability anyOf group
```

**Verification on head `16a919be3c`:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tools/planner.test.ts src/plugins/tool-descriptor-cache.test.ts src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts src/tools/availability.test.ts
  -> 101 passed (availability 11, planner 8, tool-descriptor-cache 12, tools.optional 70)

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental false
  -> exit 0
```

**What was not tested:** live gateway startup against a real external plugin package shipping malformed availability metadata.

## Compatibility note

This starts preserving plugin-authored `availability` metadata that current `main` and `v2026.6.9` ignore during descriptor capture, surfaced as warn-only diagnostics. Hidden tools behave as before; the only added behavior is the diagnostic warning. Maintainers should explicitly accept the warn-only semantics (or select an overlapping sibling implementation for #92361).

## Context capsule

This is PR1/5 for the durable runtime stack. It is intentionally docs-only: RFC, root-cause summary, durable-core boundary, validation plan, and stack sequencing before any runtime implementation is reviewed.

## Durable core stack overview

Durable core means the shared, opt-in runtime substrate that records run identity, step/event ordering, parent/child links, bounded refs, recovery states, signals/timers, and read-only inspection for long-running OpenClaw agent/session/task/subagent work. It is needed because local incidents and related public PRs show repeated coordinator-silence, stale-running-session, non-durable parent handoff, restart recovery, and bespoke durable-delivery fixes that cannot be solved cleanly by one product surface alone.

The core is intentionally below Task Flow, Workboard, plugins, sessions, and channel UI: those can project from it, but they should not own the persistence boundary. It is not a general-purpose workflow engine and does not persist raw prompts or large private payloads.

The full stack is: PR1 #101828 docs-only RFC/root-cause/canonical boundary; PR2 #102495 durable runtime core with SQLite state, lifecycle primitives, gateway/operator surfaces, QR repair, and tests; PR3 agent/session/subagent restart and upgrade-safety proof; PR4 schema lifecycle/recovery hardening; PR5 opt-in workflow worker loop. Promotion remains sequential: PR3 waits for PR1+PR2 threshold, PR4 waits for PR3, and PR5 waits for PR4.

This PR is PR1/5: it defines the boundary and root-cause plan only. ClawSweeper has already rated it 🦐 gold shrimp; the remaining question is maintainer product-direction/canonical RFC choice.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has several durable-ish records, but no shared runtime identity/lifecycle ledger for agent coordination across process, session, channel, and subagent boundaries. That gap shows up as coordinator silence, stale `running` session rows after live work disappears, non-durable parent handoffs, missed fan-in after restart, and bespoke channel/plugin durable-delivery repairs.

Related public work illustrates the same class of issue: #96853 reconciles stale running sessions; #97715 caps native subagent completion retries after permanently non-durable parent handoff; #90300 routes recovered agent-command replies through durable outbound hooks; and the older #97507/#97508 plus superseded #98717/#98718 durable stack explored overlapping boundaries. ## Summary

Adds a first-class current-turn reply metadata payload to `CurrentInboundPromptContext` so Telegram/forum reply facts survive the reply prompt/runtime handoff as structured OpenClaw metadata.

This is the Morty patch shape, polished for upstream:

- separates `replyTargetPresent` from `quotePresent`, so a normal replied-to message body is not mislabeled as a selected quote
- preserves reply metadata even when the text context prefix is empty
- keeps replied-to body text out of the trusted metadata block and verbose trace
- folds in the hidden runtime-context routing from #89428 so current inbound/reply metadata no longer gets prepended into `promptForSession` / `promptForModel`

## Related

Addresses the runtime handoff portion of #88032.

Builds on the same routing direction as #89428. This branch includes the equivalent hidden-runtime-context behavior so the reply-specific contract can be reviewed as one coherent patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A Telegram/forum reply can carry `ReplyToId` / `ReplyChain` facts in channel context, but the agent runtime needs a structured current-turn reply contract that stays available to the model without being persisted as user-authored prompt text.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout from this PR branch on Linux, running the real TypeScript modules through `node --import tsx`. The proof uses redacted Telegram/forum-style ids.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** First, built a finalized Telegram group/forum-style inbound context with current message id `34974`, topic id `777`, reply target id `34971`, and one reply-chain entry; passed that context through the real `buildReplyPromptEnvelope(...)` prompt-prelude path; rendered the current-turn runtime prefix with `buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix(...)`; checked that structured reply metadata appears before untrusted context and that the trusted reply metadata block does not include the replied-to body text.


target.title: fix(swift): keep device auth compatible with v2 gateways
target.body:
## Summary
- Add one connect-only Swift compatibility payload builder while retaining the existing v3 builder.
- Sign shared Swift and macOS wizard connect requests with the v2 canonical payload for deployed gateways that have not yet upgraded to v3 verification.
- Add a regression vector for the compatibility payload and keep the exception's restoration trigger at the builder.

## Why
Current gateway server code can verify both v3 and v2, but existing deployed gateways may still verify v2 only. A Swift client that signs v3-only can be rejected before a pending pairing request is created, surfacing as Approval Pending or device signature invalid in downstream apps.

Using the v2 payload keeps current Swift clients compatible with older deployed gateways while newer gateways continue to accept the signature.

## Security and removal window

This temporary connect-only exception leaves the nonce, signed timestamp, token, role, scopes, device ID, and public key bound by the signature. The accepted tradeoff is that `platform` and `deviceFamily` remain in the connect request but are not signature-bound by v2.

Restore `buildV3`, or add explicit signature-version negotiation, once managed and oldest-supported self-managed Gateways are expected to verify v3-before-v2. Do not reuse this helper outside the two Swift connect signers.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Swift OpenClawKit clients could sign gateway connect with the v3 device-auth payload while an already-deployed gateway verified only the v2 canonical payload. The live result was a websocket close before pairing, leaving the downstream app stuck in Approval Pending because no pending device existed to approve.

**Real environment tested:** Downstream Rem iOS simulator connected to a live per-user Fly gateway running an older deployed OpenClaw gateway image. Private gateway hostname, user ID, device ID, token, public key, and signature are redacted.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Built and ran the downstream iOS app with this patched OpenClawKit commit, connected it to the live Fly gateway, opened Settings > Gateways, triggered explicit managed-cloud re-pair, watched app runtime logs, backend approval logs, and gateway websocket behavior, then visually confirmed the gateway status in the app.

**Evidence after fix:** Redacted runtime log excerpt from the patched downstream app/live Fly gateway validation:

```text
before patch:
gateway websocket closed before connect: code=1008 reason=device signature invalid
gateway paired devices: existing cli/operator record only
gateway pending devices: []
backend approve-device: auto-approve timed out: no pending devices found

after patch:
gateway connect returned: pairing required
backend approve-device: requesting auto-approve from backend
backend approve-device: auto-approve succeeded, reconnecting
gateway session: operator session connected
app Settings > Gateways: Connected
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live gateway moved from device-signature-invalid before pairing to pairing required, backend auto-approve succeeded, the operator session connected, and the downstream app showed Settings > Gateways as Connected.

**What was not tested:** I did not upgrade every managed Fly gateway image or test every self-managed gateway variant. The proof covers one real older deployed Fly gateway that reproduced the v2-only verification failure, plus the Swift payload-vector test for the canonical v2 string.

## Validation
- SwiftPM DeviceAuthPayloadTests passed.
- Downstream iOS build and simulator run passed.
- Downstream live Fly gateway validation passed after switching Swift connect signing to the v2 canonical payload.
- Fresh maintainer SwiftFormat lint and autoreview passed after removing the redundant public v2 alias/test.
